title: Identity component and localization of a Néron lft-model
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A commutative group scheme over a base has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over that base satisfying the commutative group identities. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A scheme over a field $k$ is geometrically connected if its base change to every field extension of $k$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]; a scheme over $S$ has geometrically connected fibres if its fibre over each point $s\in S$ is geometrically connected over the residue field $\kappa(s)$. Let $H$ be a smooth separated geometrically connected commutative finite-type $K$-group [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\mathcal H$ be a Néron lft-model of $H$. A Néron lft-model of a smooth separated $K$-group $V$ means a smooth separated $S$-group $\mathcal V$, with a specified generic group isomorphism $\mathcal V_K\simeq V$, such that restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_K(X_K,V)$ for every smooth $S$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. It is only locally of finite type; finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The identity components of the geometric fibres define an open subgroup scheme $\mathcal H^0\subseteq\mathcal H$ [def-weil-open-immersion]; it is smooth separated of finite type over $S$, has geometrically connected fibres, and has generic fibre $H$. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset D$, the base change $\mathcal H_{D_{\mathfrak m}}$ is a Néron lft-model of $H$ over $\operatorname{Spec}D_{\mathfrak m}$, with the same generic identification. Its open subgroup of fibrewise identity components is $(\mathcal H^0)_{D_{\mathfrak m}}$. The notation $D_{\mathfrak m}$ denotes localization at the complement of $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: BLR 10.1 Definition 1 and the paragraph immediately following it, printed pp.289–290 (PDF pp.295–296): localization compatibility and finite type of the identity component. proof.text: Write $G=\mathcal H$. Its geometric fibres are smooth: apply [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1) locally where the relative dimension is constant. Thus they are locally of finite type. Let $N\subseteq|G|$ be the union of the ordinary fibre components containing the identity. The section-component base-change theorem [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] identifies its inverse image in every geometric fibre with that fibre's identity component. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] over each algebraically closed residue field: these components are open-and-closed, geometrically irreducible, quasi-compact subgroup schemes. In particular the ordinary component $C_s\subseteq G_s$ is quasi-compact too: it is the continuous image of its geometric component under field-extension projection. That projection is surjective, since for a point with residue field $L$ the tensor product $L\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\overline{\kappa(s)}$ is nonzero (tensor a basis of the field extension) and hence has a prime ideal. These assertions apply to locally finite type fibres; no quasi-compactness of $G$ is assumed.

Fix $s\in S$. Both $e(S)$ and $C_s$ are quasi-compact, so finitely many affine opens of $G$ cover them; let $W$ be their union. The section factors through $W$. This open restriction is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. It is separated: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $G$, using [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change]. As $W$ is quasi-compact over the affine base, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over $S$. Thus [lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-open] applies to $W\to S$. Its section-component locus $W^0$ is open in $G$, is contained in $N$, and contains all of $C_s$: the component of $e(s)$ in $W_s$ is exactly $C_s$, since $C_s\subset W_s$ and connected subsets of $W_s$ containing $e(s)$ remain connected in $G_s$. Varying $s$ shows that $N$ is open. Give it the restricted structure sheaf.

source.place: Tags 055R (lemma-connected-along-section-open), 01VC and 01VA (open smooth restriction), 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion); finite affine-open unions

proof.text: The multiplication, inverse and identity maps factor through the open subscheme $N$: at every geometric point this is the subgroup assertion of [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component]. A map into a scheme factors through an open subscheme exactly when its point image lies in that open, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. The group identities restrict because the open inclusion is a monomorphism. Smoothness follows from [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], and separatedness from the restricted diagonal and [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change]. The geometric fibres are the components identified in Step 1, so are geometrically connected. The generic component is all of $H$, because $H$ is geometrically connected; hence $N_K=H$ with the specified generic identification.

source.place: Tag 055M and groupoids.tex Tag 0B7R; open-factorization and restriction of the group operations

proof.text: Choose a finite union $U$ of affine opens of $N$ containing $e(S)$. It is quasi-compact and its every geometric fibre is a nonempty open in the irreducible scheme $N_{\bar s}$, by [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component]. The difference map $q:U\times_SU\to N$, $(u,v)\mapsto uv^{-1}$, is surjective on points. Indeed for any geometric point $g$ of $N_{\bar s}$, the two nonempty opens $U_{\bar s}$ and $gU_{\bar s}$ meet by irreducibility. A point of their intersection, after extension to its residue field, writes $u=gv$ with $u,v\in U$, so $g=uv^{-1}$ and the original point lifts to the source of $q$. The source is quasi-compact: pairs of the finitely many affine opens of $U$ give a finite cover by affine fibre products over the affine $S$, using [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Pulling back an open cover of $N$ along the continuous surjection $q$ and taking a finite subcover proves $N$ quasi-compact. It is locally of finite type by smoothness, so [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives finite type. This proves the required finiteness without assuming that the whole lft-model is of finite type.

source.place: BLR 10.1 following Definition 1, printed p.290: finite type by the surjective group-law map from a fibrewise dense open; groupoids.tex Tag 0B7R; schemes.tex Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes

proof.text: Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, put $R=D_{\mathfrak m}$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $G_T=G\times_ST$. Smoothness survives this base change: locally in the source the relative dimension of a smooth morphism is constant, and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1) applies there. Separatedness survives because the new diagonal is the base change of the old diagonal, a closed immersion by [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change]. The group operations base change by the fibre-product universal property. Localization does not change the fraction field: the maps $(a/s)/ (b/t)\mapsto at/(sb)$ and $a/b\mapsto(a/1)/(b/1)$ are inverse. Thus $(G_T)_K=H$ with the original generic identification. It remains to prove its mapping property.

source.place: morphisms.tex Tags 01VB and 02NK (smooth base change); closed-immersion base change; BLR 10.1 localization

proof.text: Let $X\to T$ be smooth and $u_K:X_K\to H$ a morphism. On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$, the map $R\to B$ is smooth in the affine-ring sense, by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Write $R=\varinjlim_{f\notin\mathfrak m}D[1/f]$: any finite list of fractions lies in the stage with denominator their product, directly from [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-filtered-colimit-descent] to obtain $f\notin\mathfrak m$ and a smooth $D[1/f]$-algebra $B_f$ with $B\simeq R\otimes_{D[1/f]}B_f$. Put $V_f=\operatorname{Spec}B_f$, smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}D[1/f]$ by the reverse implication of that same equivalence. The base map $\operatorname{Spec}D[1/f]\hookrightarrow S$ is smooth (apply [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] to the identity of $S$), so $V_f\to S$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Its generic fibre is $V_K$, since both bases have fraction field $K$. The original Néron mapping property extends $u_K|_{V_K}$ to $V_f\to G$. Pull back to $T$ to obtain $u_V:V\to G_T$. Only the test scheme descends here; no finite-presentation hypothesis on $G$ is used.

source.place: algebra.tex Tag 0CAQ, lemma-smooth-descends-through-colimit; morphisms.tex Tag 01VA, lemma-composition-smooth; BLR 10.1 localization; Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize; Tag 01VC, lemma-open-immersion-smooth

proof.text: The generic-fibre map of every smooth $T$-scheme $Y$ is scheme-theoretically dominant, meaning injective on the structure sheaf. Indeed on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$, the ring map $R\to A$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Tensoring the injection $R\hookrightarrow K$ with $A$ gives $A\hookrightarrow K\otimes_RA$ by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; this is precisely injectivity on affine sections, hence on the sheaf. Apply [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] to the separated $T$-scheme $G_T$: two maps from $Y$ agreeing generically are equal. The maps $u_V$ of Step 6 therefore agree on every overlap, which is smooth as an open of $X$ by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. They glue to a map $X\to G_T$ because scheme morphisms glue on an open cover (glue the continuous maps and their maps of restricted structure sheaves). The same uniqueness argument applies to $X$ itself, with no quasi-compactness assumption. Thus restriction on Hom is bijective, and $G_T$ is the required Néron lft-model.

source.place: algebra.tex Tags 00TA and 00SL (smooth implies flat); separated uniqueness on a scheme-theoretically dominant restriction; BLR 10.1 localization; Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] to the structure map $G\to S$, its identity section, and $T\to S$. Its equality of component loci says that the neutral subset of $G_T$ is exactly the inverse image of $N$. Both are open by Step 2, which applies to this smooth separated group over the affine Noetherian base $T$ as well. An open subscheme is the restriction of the structure sheaf to its open subset [def-weil-open-immersion], so identical subsets give identical open subschemes. Their group structures restrict the same operations. Consequently $(\mathcal H^0)_T=(\mathcal H_T)^0$, as asserted.

I read all 8 steps against the cited statements. The item statement is unchanged and there are no new nodes. The item was unsplit with no proof on the base, so this is not a re-split. The local BLR 10.1 PDF is missing (marked WANTED). I checked the statement clause by clause against BLR 10.1 Definition 1 and the paragraph after it: Néron lft-model with the mapping property for every smooth S-scheme, the open subgroup H^0 of finite type, and localization. Step 1: the section-component cartesian lemma at a geometric point plus the identity-component lemma over an algebraically closed field. The projection from the geometric fibre is surjective, so C_s is quasi-compact. Step 2: the openness lemma is applied only to a quasi-compact union W of affine opens; W is separated via the base-changed diagonal. The maximality argument shows W^0 lies in N and contains C_s. Step 3: the subgroup and open-factorization arguments are correct. Step 4: the difference map U×U→N is surjective because N_{s̄} is irreducible, and this gives finite type without assuming G is quasi-compact. I tested it on the split-torus lft-model and on the trivial group. Steps 5–7: descent of smooth algebras along D_m = colim D[1/f], smooth composition and flatness give generic scheme-theoretic dominance. Uniqueness for a separated target then lets the maps glue for any smooth X. Step 8: the cartesian lemma identifies the neutral part of G_T with the preimage of H^0. Unstated one-liners: W→S and N→S are quasi-compact because W and N are Noetherian, and id_S is smooth. Both are elementary. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-smooth-composition is the generic Mathlib-matched fact that a composite of smooth morphisms is smooth (Stacks 01VA). It is outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions, so I accept it. I also accept the tool_uses: general scheme lemmas used exactly as stated. No duplicates found; the field identity-component nodes with stronger hypotheses were rightly not used.
